takeaway: The ulnar nerve supplies the interossei, so its injury at the elbow weakens finger abduction and adduction.

lines.text: An 18-year-old man has a posterior dislocation of his left elbow.
lines.say: An eighteen-year-old man has a posterior dislocation of his left elbow.

lines.text: The joint has been pushed out of place, backwards.
He has decreased sensation and weakness in his left first web space.
He also has weak adduction and abduction of his fingers.
The nerve injured at his elbow is the ulnar nerve.
The ulnar nerve supplies the interossei, the muscles that spread and close the fingers.
So weak finger abduction and adduction after this dislocation means ulnar nerve injury.
